De Moivre: \((\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)^n=\cos n\theta+i\sin n\theta\). Here \(n\theta=\frac{5 \pi}{4}\), so the value is \(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}i\).

Locate the point \((-3,\,-3)\) and find its quadrant. It is in the third quadrant, so \(\theta=-(\pi-\alpha)\) with \(\alpha=\tan^{-1}|y/x|\). The principal argument is \(- \frac{3 \pi}{4}\), which lies in \((-\pi,\pi]\).
